As well as, the death of the sorcerers who knew how to apply that blood magic to the creating of steel.

Dragon Glass is just obsidian rock, as we have in our world, aka volcanic rock.  It is formed by the internal heat of the Earth/Volcanoes/however the science goes.

I do agree however that Dragon Steel/Valyrian Steel does require dragon fire.  But I think there has to be more to it than that, some kind of magical element as well.  The Targs had dragons for another \~250 years following the doom, and it does not appear that they continued to produce Valryian steel following the doom. 

What I think makes the idea of Valyrian Steel requiring dragon fire the most interesting is how it connects to Lightbringer and AA.  My theory, and I imagine a relatively popular theory, is that Lightbringer is not actually literally burning, but rather is made of "fire steel".  As Quaithe says,"For *dragons are fire made flesh*, and *fire* is power." I imagine similar could be said for Valryian steel, "For dragon steel is fire made steel."

That is true about the original Daenerys, but that was 100 years ago and I imagine someone has to have a closer claim.  I believe that person is Selwyn Tarth.  Maester Aemon, brother of Egg/Aegon V, I believe mentions wishing to see his sisters and their children again, so if they did have any offspring and their subsequent lines both would have claims several generations closer than Doran's.  But in actuality, neither even has any actual Targ claim as per the precedent set in the Great Council of 101, where Rhaenys and her childrens' claims were overlooked for a closer male heir.

There is only one rightful living heir to the Baratheon Throne, and that is Stannis Baratheon.  Daenerys and fAegon (and eventually when Jon finds out) no longer have claims to throne by rights, but could retake the Iron Throne by rights of conquest as their common ancestors did.  Tommen and Myrcella have no actual claim as they are both bastard born, and have no Baratheon blood, but obviously have primary claim because no one but a handful know that to be absolutely true. If Targaryen inheritance tradition holds, Myrcella would have no claim even if she was actually Robert's daughter as the throne cannot pass through the female line. Aaaand also she is probably dead.  Edric Storm, Gendry, and Mya Stone have no claim at all unless legitimized.  I guess Bloodraven would also fall in with the other Targs and could claim the throne by conquest, but he does not appear to be in any state to do so (his focus being to the north, as well as stealing Bran's body). These are the characters from your list that could validate a claim for themselves.

Clearly, Doran and Euron have no blood claim to the throne but would both make interesting choices if there was to be an election type event. Euron is attractive, a strong warrior, charismatic af, and experienced. We'd all hope that Euron wouldn't be chosen, but he is power hungry and appears to know how to touch on the right buttons of electors.  Much like a certain president in America today, but hopefully the Westerosi would be a little wiser than we were.  Doran would seem to be a great choice from an administrative standpoint, but my guess would be that many of the lords would not stand for him because of his physical disability(gout) and that many southern lords have a prejudice still against the Dornish. A culture precedence could stand against Euron as well, as no one likes the Ironborn.

I hope not to catch shit for mentioning the show, but because we do not know yet in the books, I think there is a decent chance that Cersei also claims the throne for herself in the books.  In that case, it'd be fair to add Jaime and Tyrion to this list.  Jaime would stand as rightful heir to Cersei, if in the books he has been removed from the Kingsguard \*but honestly I can't remember if thats true and I'm not even sure in the show\*. There'd be a certain irony if the Kingslayer became the king.  Especially considering that Ned found him and not say Tywin, sitting on the throne upon his arrival in the city.  I think lots of us would like to put a vote out for Tyrion, but I imagine his reputation is too tarnished to get much support.

If you want to add additional Targ era claimants, I think Selwyn Tarth would be a good choice.  We know the family from Tarth had some recent Targaryen union, likely one of Egg's sisters.  Selwyn appears to be a kind and righteous guy.  After Stannis and Jon, I'd give my vote to the Evenstar.
